Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the context. We can map this into a two-track plan: a) staged hydration (priority-first backfill + late-binding seeds) and b) rerank evaluation harness to measure lift vs your keyword model. High level proposed deliverables:

1) Pre-flight (3 business days)
  - ingest sample snapshot (we’ll validate schema + tokenization).
  - run sizing run to estimate vector DB shard count and per-hour write throughput.
  - cost delta estimate for full vs staged backfill.

2) Pilot wave (2 weeks)
  - wave 0: 50k high-value docs, run rerank A/B against baseline.
  - wave 1: progressive 10% increments to 100% of high-value buckets.

3) Production cutover (phased)
  - throttle-controlled full backfill with prefix caching enabled to reduce infer cost.
  - smoke tests and rerank regression gating (precision@5, NDCG metrics).

I’ve attached a tentative workbook (embed_backfill_plan.xlsx) and the rerank eval template. Let me know 2-3 windows for a 30–45 min kickoff this week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

SG — I’ll take DB sizing. Initial notes:
- For 18M small docs (~average 150 tokens) we recommend 6 primary shards with 2x replication for throughput; estimate writes peak ~1.2M docs/hour for an aggressive backfill.
- Recommend staged priority backfill: seed top 10% of documents by traffic, then run wave-based expansion. Late-binding is attractive because it minimizes immediate IO and infer costs, but increases tail-latency complexity when queries hit uncached items.
- TTL: set 180d for ephemeral seeds during pilot, remove TTL post-cutover.

I’ll populate vector-db-sizing.csv with throughput assumptions and a throttled schedule for the full backfill. No blockers on our side other than confirming maintenance window for their primary region.

—Ben
